items.title: Sidney MacDonald, Kitchener
notes: S. MacDonald provided living expertise on being unhoused as a woman in the Region of Waterloo and expressed concern that there is not a dedicated housing shelter for women and non-binary individuals. They requested that a dedicated space for a women's shelter be created in the Region of Waterloo.

items.title: Atlas Ruin-Bloom, Kitchener
notes: A. Ruin-Bloom expressed concern that gender neutral spaces can be intimidating and unsafe for women and non-binary individuals and that housing shelters need dedicated spaces to accommodate diverse individuals to ensure all residents feel safe and secure.

items.title: Laura Coakley, Kitchener
notes: L. Coakley expressed support for the proposed women and gender diverse housing shelter at 84 Frederick Street as it is a necessity for such a large population in Ontario.

items.title: Bailey Howell, SASC of Waterloo Region/Services Housing in the Province
notes: B. Howell provided the lived experiences of various community members that faced gender based violence and safety concerns while using the shelter system.

items.title: Eddy Grignon, Kitchener
notes: E. Grignon provided a lived experience related to housing shelters and how important these community services are in the Region of Waterloo.

items.title: Ryan Murdock, Kitchener
notes: R. Murdock expressed concern that the YMCA Women's Shelter was closed and that Region of Waterloo purchased the property without a designated plan to continue utilizing the property as a women shelter. They also suggested that funding and Staffing should be increased for housing shelters.

items.title: Julie Kalbfleisch and Jillian Lawrie, Coalition Against Women's Homelessness
notes:
J. Kalbfleisch and J. Lawrie expressed support for the report CSD-HOU-24-015, 84 Frederick Operating Model to establish a women's shelter and the importance of increasing women's shelters throughout the Region. J. Lawrie noted their lived experience and how fundamental services are that are centered around gender diverse individuals in the community. 

In response to the Committee, Ashley Schuitema, member of the Coalition Against Women's Homelessness, explained that any analysis and solutions need to include a gender based considerations and statistics such as the point in time count.

Peter Sweeney, Commissioner of Community of Services, noted that the Plan to End Chronic Homelessness was based on lived experience and providing solutions through an equity lens with community partners. He further noted that the Staff report listed under item 9.1.1. recommends that 84 Frederick St. become a women and gender diverse housing shelter.

Following the delegations the Committee considered a motion to resume closed session.

items.title: Consent Agenda

items.title: CSD-HOU-24-015, 84 Frederick Operating Model
notes:
P. Sweeney provided a brief overview of report CSD-HOU-24-015, 84 Frederick Operating Model, including community feedback on the proposed operating model as provided in Appendix A. He highlighted that the proposed operating model was formed with community consultation to address the urgent need for a women and gender diverse housing shelter. The report was presented for information.

In response to the Committee, P. Sweeney clarified that the King Street housing shelter will be closing on March 31, 2025. He further clarified that 84 Frederick St. housing shelter will not be an exact replacement for the King St. shelter, however, the new shelter will be a fundamental element of the Regional housing system. The Committee requested that the neighbouring community surrounding the King Street housing shelter be kept informed on next steps related to the closure of the shelter.

Responding to the Committee, P. Sweeney confirmed that the YWCA is an independent organization that made an independent decision to sell 84 Frederick Street. He further confirmed that Staff are working to ensure equitable outcomes for all community organizations based on community needs set out in the Plan to End Chronic Homelessness.

The Committee expressed support for the proposed model and Kelly-Anne Salerno, Associate Director, Housing Operations and Administration, explained that the proposed model is different from previous models as its based on lived experience feedback and housing outcomes. She further explained that there will be dedicated single occupancy and the renovations are focused on creating more single occupancy spaces, however, need of spaces may cause shared spaces to be necessary. 

In response to the Committee, K. Salerno confirmed that the model was based on community feedback and that Staff are striving to collaborate with the Plan to End Chronic Homelessness co-creator group, individuals with lived expertise, and ongoing feedback from shelter residents. P. Sweeney further confirmed that the proposed operating model will continue to be developed based on community needs and in coordination with the Plan to End Chronic Homelessness and Regional Council consultation.

items.title: Strategic Priority - Equitable Services and Opportunities
CSD-IPP-24-001, Waterloo Region Immigration Profile 2024
notes:
Tara Bedard, Executive Director Immigration Partnership, provided a presentation on the report CSD-IPP-24-001, Waterloo Region Immigration Profile 2024. A copy of the presentation is attached to the agenda. She highlighted the significant increase of new permanent and temporary resident arrivals in the Region of Waterloo and that immigration, including secondary migration, has been driving population growth. She further highlighted the demographics of immigration which is driving Regional diversity. Community challenges continue to be cost of living, housing costs, and employment. She noted that the Region of Waterloo continues to develop services to better serve the community including providing language interpretation and translation enables service and engagement access.

Ernest Osei, Immigration Partnership Council Member, provided a lived expertise account and expressed the importance of immigration supports and adhering to the Regional strategic priority of growing with care. 

In response to the Committee, T. Bedard confirmed that the statistics listed in Appendix A: Figure 20 are provided by data sources including Statistics Canada. The Committee expressed concern with Figure 27 that illustrates that unemployment is higher in racialized Canadian born individuals than racialized immigrants.

The Committee requested that Staff report back on the impact of the increase of immigration on community support services, such as lunch programs, international students, and housing shelters.

Responding to the Committee, Monica Vythilingam, Epidemiologist, clarified that census data is released every five years and the next census will be in 2026. 

The Committee noted that ongoing data will be essential to guide Council and Staff and that budget considerations for service needs to continue to be at the forefront. 

Received for information.

items.title: Strategic Priority - Resilient and Future Ready Organization
EES-FFM-24-005, 651 Concession Road, Cambridge Redevelopment - Paramedic Services
notes:
Jennifer Rose, Commissioner Engineering & Environmental Services, introduced the report EES-FFM-24-005, 651 Concession Road, Cambridge Redevelopment - Paramedic Services. She highlighted that Staff determined that the property use was ideal for paramedic services and will require an increase in the capital budget.

In response to the Committee, P. Sweeney explained the removal of the current housing service is included in the transition plan. He further explained that the use of the space as affordable housing and a childcare center would have both financial and functional implications that Staff would not currently recommend. Specifically, Staff would not recommend as it would be costly, safety considerations, delays to paramedic services, and Staff limitations to support these facilities. 

Responding to the Committee, J. Rose confirmed that Staff can look into configuring the building structure to be able to accommodate childcare and affordable housing in the future.

The Committee expressed support for the proposed site location based on community need and population density.
